flags.why: This is a formal military term, so leaving it untagged misrepresents its register.
The writing-system sense remains current in scholarly usage and is not archaic; see [the dictionary entry](https://hvdic.thivien.net/hv/v%C4%83n%20t%E1%BB%B1).
Learners today are more likely to encounter the writing-system sense than the old property-deed sense.
The example uses the separate word trơ trọi rather than demonstrating trơ itself.
flags.fix: Mọi người đã về hết, chỉ còn trơ lại một mình anh ấy. = Everyone has gone home, leaving him all alone.

flags.why: This expression belongs to formal or careful speech and needs a register label.
Gò means a raised mound of land, not an island; see [the dictionary entry](https://www.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/G%C3%B2).
The common sense of forcing someone or oneself into constraints is missing; see [the dictionary entry](https://www.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/G%C3%B2).
flags.fix: Add a verb sense: to constrain; to force into a prescribed pattern; example: Tôi không muốn gò mình theo ý người khác. = I don't want to force myself to conform to other people's wishes.

flags.why: Ca nhạc does not mean musicality, and the rare tag cannot make this invented sense valid; see [the dictionary entry](https://www.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/Ca_nh%E1%BA%A1c).
Phức hợp is not a verb meaning to mix ingredients; see [the dictionary entry](https://www.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/Ph%E1%BB%A9c_h%E1%BB%A3p).
